vegetation: Annually burned tallgrass prairie, tower in ungrazed watershed 1D. Dominant perennial C4 grasses: Andropogon gerardii, Panicum virgatum, Schizachyrium scoparium and Sorghastrum nutans; subdominant C3 grasses, forbs and woody plants occur in Konza prairie.
observed_composition: Graminoids, almost all grasses, account for 96% of herbaceous biomass in watershed 1D; this is NOT a measured C4 percentage or a ground-area fraction.
observed_pft_summary: Grass-dominated biomass with C4 dominants; exact C3:C4 and woody/shrub ground-cover shares unresolved.
denominator: Oven-dried herbaceous biomass; excludes woody biomass and bare ground. 96% graminoids, approximately 4% non-graminoid herbaceous biomass by complement.
observation_period: 1984–2010 end-of-growing-season quadrat clipping; source published 2012. Tower/watershed identity cross-checked in Brunsell et al. 2017.
spatial_scope: Watershed 1D, upland and lowland positions; five 20×50 cm quadrats in each of four transects per landscape position. Watershed sample, not half-hourly flux-footprint-weighted vegetation.
bare_ground: Not quantified; 4% herbaceous residual is not bare ground.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-Kon site overview; Craine et al. (2012), Timing of climate variability and grassland productivity, PNAS 109:3401–3405, doi:10.1073/pnas.1118438109; Brunsell et al. (2017), Assessing the Roles of Fire Frequency and Precipitation in Determining Woody Plant Expansion in Central U.S. Grasslands, doi:10.1002/2017JG004046
source_locator: Official Overview: Vegetation IGBP and Description; Craine Materials and Methods paragraph beginning Graminoid ANPP; Brunsell section 2.1 Field Data identifies US-KON as watershed 1D and names dominant C4 grasses.
candidate_pft: C4 grass dominant; C3 herbaceous contribution and any woody contribution unquantified. No exact percentage vector proposed.
candidate_basis: Observed grass biomass dominance plus primary site-specific C4 dominant species list; species-to-functional mapping is an interpretation, not a new cover observation.
uncertainties: Official site description mentions bison/cattle introductions at the broader station; Brunsell explicitly calls the tower watershed ungrazed. Use tower-watershed evidence rather than station-wide management. Biomass share is not fractional cover, leaf area or FATES carbon share.
next_evidence: Retrieve contemporaneous watershed 1D species-cover records (Konza LTER vegetation transects) and the release BADM VEG_COVER/VEG_PCT records; quantify bare/rock/litter separately.

vegetation: Before August 2020: almost entirely Pinus ponderosa overstory with scattered Calocedrus decurrens; sparse Purshia tridentata and Arctostaphylos patula understory. Fire, salvage logging and footprint relocation then changed the site.
observed_composition: Pre-fire overstory peak LAI 2.1 m2/m2; understory LAI 0.2 m2/m2; approximately 339 trees/ha. No observed tree-species or ground-area percentage was found. These LAIs must not be converted into ground-cover percentages.
observed_pft_summary: Pre-fire evergreen needleleaf overstory plus broadleaf shrub understory; post-fire and post-logging composition unresolved.
denominator: LAI per ground area, separate canopy strata; species dominance qualitative.
observation_period: Pre-fire site description January 2002–August 2020. Green Ridge Fire crossed site 2020-08-20; salvage logging late March–late April 2021; primary flux system moved August 2022.
spatial_scope: Pre-fire stand around original tower; almost all trees within flux footprint logged except a smaller low-severity area; 2022 tower centers on salvage/regenerating footprint.
bare_ground: Official description reports ash/bare soil in intensely burned patches, but does not provide a footprint-wide bare-ground percentage.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-Me2 site overview and AmeriFlux BASE US-Me2 dataset description, doi:10.17190/AMF/1246076
source_locator: Overview Description: Site Description before Fire; dataset description headings Green Ridge Fire and Salvage Logging, including August 2022 flux-system move.
candidate_pft: Pre-fire temperate evergreen needleleaf tree dominant, plus broadleaf shrubs; distinct 2020–2021 burned and post-2021 regenerating states required. No stationary exact vector proposed.
candidate_basis: Official species list and disturbance chronology; functional mapping provisional.
uncertainties: ENF category is not a cover measurement. The 2002–2022 forcing release crosses fire and salvage logging. Peak overstory and understory LAIs are not species fractions; current description is not time-invariant vegetation truth.
next_evidence: Acquire pre/post-fire plot or lidar species and cover inventories and 2021/2022 footprint maps; date-match each modeled period and quantify live vegetation, dead boles, bare soil and regrowth separately.

vegetation: Open young Pinus ponderosa regeneration after 1979 fire, salvage logging, planting in 1986 and additional planting in 1990. Scattered Purshia tridentata and grasses, predominantly Bromus tectorum, form understory.
observed_composition: Ruehr et al. report 2010 summer overstory half-sided LAI 0.8 m2/m2, understory estimated LAI 0.1 m2/m2 and 162 trees/ha. Official site currently states overstory LAI 0.6 for 2010. Neither source supplies a species/ground-cover percentage vector.
observed_pft_summary: Evergreen needleleaf trees plus broadleaf deciduous shrubs and C3 grasses; their area shares are unmeasured in the read sources.
denominator: Leaf area per ground area and tree density; no percent-cover denominator.
observation_period: 2010–2011 field observations in Ruehr et al. 2014; stand 22–26 years old then. Official overview describes an approximately 20-year-old stand.
spatial_scope: US-Me6 study stand; biomass inventory four plots of 17 m radius and LAI on two transects. No annual flux-footprint weighting given.
bare_ground: Open stand and gaps are described; ground bare-soil/rock/litter fractions not quantified.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-Me6 site overview; Ruehr et al. (2014), Effects of heat and drought on carbon and water dynamics in a regenerating semi-arid pine forest: a combined experimental and modeling approach, Biogeosciences 11:4139–4156, doi:10.5194/bg-11-4139-2014
source_locator: Official Overview Description; Ruehr pp. 4140–4141 sections 2.1 Study site and 2.2 Observational data. Paper section 2.3.1 treats understory as pine for model simplification; that is not field composition.
candidate_pft: Temperate evergreen needleleaf trees + deciduous broadleaf shrub + C3 grass, unknown fractions.
candidate_basis: Field species list and functional physiology; no inferred percent of ground from LAI.
uncertainties: 0.6 official versus 0.8 paper overstory LAI discrepancy; planted 1986 versus simplified official reforested 1990 description. Stand has regenerated through 2010–2025 release period, so early-stand LAI is not timeless.
next_evidence: Release BADM species cover/LAI time series and plot survey maps; resolve LAI definition/date and obtain actual tree crown, shrub, grass and bare-ground cover for modeled periods.

vegetation: Secondary deciduous broadleaf forest; Acer saccharum, Liriodendron tulipifera and Quercus spp. are major canopy genera.
observed_composition: Denham et al. report Acer saccharum + Liriodendron tulipifera + Quercus spp. together account for 75% of stand basal area; remaining 25% is not species-resolved in this read source. All three named groups map to deciduous broadleaf trees.
observed_pft_summary: At least the named 75% of basal area is deciduous broadleaf; no complete cover or PFT-area vector established.
denominator: Stand tree basal area; 75% combined named species/genera, 25% unspecified residual. Not percent of ground area.
observation_period: Site characterization in Denham et al. 2021, accepted 2020. Original basal-area census date is not explicit in the cited description; sap-flow study includes 2012 drought.
spatial_scope: Morgan Monroe tower stand, Indiana; basal-area survey extent not specified in the read source.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-MMS site overview; Denham et al. (2021), Eastern US deciduous tree species respond dissimilarly to declining soil moisture but similarly to rising evaporative demand, Tree Physiology 41:944–959, doi:10.1093/treephys/tpaa153
source_locator: Official Overview Vegetation IGBP; Denham p. 946 Site description paragraph beginning Morgan Monroe State Forest.
candidate_pft: Temperate deciduous broadleaf tree dominant; residual flora and understory unquantified. Do not assign 100% from DBF label.
candidate_basis: Observed 75% combined basal area and deciduous species identities.
uncertainties: A historical 2000 stand table exists, but it was not independently read in an official/author-hosted full text during this pass; no historical table percentages are substituted here. Exact survey date and full 25% residual need verification.
next_evidence: Retrieve original Schmid et al. 2000 Table 1 and modern tower plot census/BADM; preserve census year, sampled basal area and species residual before deriving PFT composition.
functional_group_percent_basis: Stand tree basal area; 75% combined named species/genera, 25% unspecified residual. vegetation: Second-growth upland oak–hickory forest with Acer saccharum understory and Juniperus virginiana, including locally disturbed areas.
observed_composition: Momen et al. 2017 reports basal-area shares approximately Quercus alba 39%, Juniperus virginiana 10%, Quercus velutina 9%, Carya ovata 7%, Acer saccharum 7%; sum of listed approximate shares 72%, residual approximately 28% unspecified. Geron et al. report canopy cover around tower 85–92%.
observed_pft_summary: Named deciduous broadleaf taxa total approximately 62% of basal area; named evergreen needleleaf Juniperus approximately 10%; approximately 28% unresolved. These are partial BA shares, not ground cover.
denominator: Species shares: total stand basal area. Separate 85–92%: total canopy cover around tower. Never merge these denominators or call canopy openings bare soil.
observation_period: Momen water-potential data 2004–2010; stand-composition census date not separately given. Geron site context for PINOT NOIR 2012 published 2016.
spatial_scope: Baskett/MOFLUX tower stand in Missouri; canopy-cover description around tower. Species BA survey extent not explicit in Momen paragraph.
bare_ground: Not quantified. Canopy cover 85–92% implies canopy gaps, not 8–15% bare ground; understory/litter/rock may occupy gaps.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-MOz site overview; Momen et al. (2017), Interacting Effects of Leaf Water Potential and Biomass on Vegetation Optical Depth, doi:10.1002/2017JG004145; Geron et al. (2016), Large drought-induced variations in oak leaf volatile organic compound emissions during PINOT NOIR 2012, doi:10.1016/j.chemosphere.2015.11.086
source_locator: Momen p. 3034 (PDF p. 4) MOFLUX paragraph and Table 1; Geron p. 9 (PDF p. 2), section 1.1 Site description. Geron Table 1 distinguishes MOFLUX footprint from regional FIA, so regional FIA values must not substitute tower values.
candidate_pft: Temperate deciduous broadleaf dominant with observed evergreen needleleaf component; retain unresolved remainder. No full site-area vector proposed.
candidate_basis: Species-to-PFT grouping of reported BA shares; 62/10/28 are approximate partial stand-BA accounting, not FATES area or carbon fractions.
uncertainties: Strong drought and mortality in measurement period can alter composition. IGBP DBF does not establish absence of evergreen trees. Residual species remain unresolved; observation dates differ across sources.
next_evidence: Read complete MOFLUX inventory/BADM species table with census date and footprint map; identify residual 28%, update mortality and crown-cover fractions.

vegetation: Pinus edulis and Juniperus monosperma woodland with dominant herbaceous Bouteloua gracilis, a perennial C4 grass.
observed_composition: Official site reports Pinus edulis + Juniperus monosperma make up >95% of tree cover; total tree cover approximately 60%. Separate species shares within the pair and herbaceous cover are not given.
observed_pft_summary: Evergreen conifer canopy dominates tree cover; C4 grass understory present. Percent of tree cover and percent of ground must remain separate.
denominator: >95% uses total tree cover as denominator; approximately 60% uses site ground/canopy cover area. These statements are not a complete mutually exclusive PFT-area partition.
observation_period: Official undated overview; piñon mortality began July 2013 and continued through 2015. No census date supplied for 60% or >95% statements.
spatial_scope: Mesa approximately 25 km south of Mountainair, New Mexico, around flux site; source does not specify cover inventory plot or footprint weighting.
bare_ground: Not measured. Approximately 40% outside tree canopy may include grass, shrubs, litter, bare soil or rock and must not be assigned to bare ground or C4 grass wholesale.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-Mpj site overview, Mountainair Pinyon-Juniper Woodland
source_locator: Overview Description paragraphs on >95% tree cover, approximately 60% total tree cover, Bouteloua gracilis, and 2013–2015 piñon mortality.
candidate_pft: Evergreen needleleaf tree plus C4 grass, unknown within-pair and understory shares. Disturbance-era states required; no exact vector proposed.
candidate_basis: Official species identity and two cover measures; functional interpretation provisional.
uncertainties: Piñon drought/ips mortality affected 2013–2015; juniper unaffected per official overview. BIF labels ENF/OSH/WSA retained in Batch03 history; current WSA is context, not a numerical observation. Juniper model classification may depend on parameter-set growth form.
next_evidence: Retrieve before/after-mortality tree crown/species inventories and understory/bare cover; verify geographic footprint and census years before converting any proportions.

vegetation: Semiarid mature second-growth mixed conifer forest dominated by Pseudotsuga menziesii, Pinus ponderosa and Pinus strobiformis; little understory vegetation.
observed_composition: Primary site papers identify the three major evergreen conifers, but no stand-wide species or functional percentage was verified. Yang et al. describe the sampled 1.5 ha catchment as codominated by P. menziesii and P. ponderosa; codominant is not evidence for 50:50.
observed_pft_summary: Evergreen needleleaf forest; precise species shares and minor woody/herbaceous shares unresolved.
denominator: None: species dominance descriptions, not percent composition.
observation_period: Tower operating since 2009; cited JGR study published 2022. Selective thinning in 2012 noted by Yang et al. 2020.
spatial_scope: Mt Bigelow tower forest, Santa Catalina Mountains, Arizona. Yang 1.5 ha zero-order-basin catchment lies within statistical tower footprint; it is a sample scope, not the entire footprint.
bare_ground: Not quantified; little understory does not imply quantified bare soil.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-MtB site overview; Javadian et al. source_locator: Official Overview ENF; Javadian Site description paragraph lists three dominant conifers and little understory; Yang Materials and methods, Site description describes codominants, 2012 thinning and 1.5 ha footprint catchment.
candidate_pft: Temperate evergreen needleleaf tree dominant; no exact fractional vector supported.
candidate_basis: All named dominant canopy species are evergreen conifers; no conversion of ENF label to observed 100% cover.
uncertainties: Sample catchment and full tower footprint can differ; 2012 thinning and later climate stress may change canopy structure. No numeric composition or bare-ground estimate verified.
next_evidence: Tower-footprint tree inventory with species basal area/crown cover, thinning records and ground-cover survey; distinguish sampled tree counts from forest abundance.

vegetation: Managed Pinus taeda plantation established 1992; subdominant/understory Acer rubrum and other broadleaf understory occur.
observed_composition: Official source verifies loblolly pine plantation and disturbance chronology. No complete numeric species/functional fraction verified. Noormets et al. report seasonal LAI 3.9–4.3 m2/m2 at growing-season maximum and 2.4–2.8 in winter, partly due to Acer rubrum leaf fall; these are not PFT shares.
observed_pft_summary: Evergreen needleleaf plantation overstory with deciduous broadleaf subdominants/understory; exact shares unquantified.
denominator: Total projected LAI per ground area; no species fraction supplied in the read primary passage.
observation_period: Noormets 2012 study includes 2005–2009; official chronology: stand established 1992, drought and management in 2007, thinned October 2009, fertilization January 2011 eastern half and October 2012 whole site.
spatial_scope: Parker Tract lower coastal plain North Carolina tower plantation. Noormets LAI on four of thirteen vegetation survey plots; no footprint-weighted species percentages supplied.
bare_ground: Not quantified; thinning creates canopy gaps without establishing bare-soil area.

source_locator: Official dataset Description; Noormets p. 3188 paragraph on US-NC2 LAI and subdominant/understory Acer rubrum.

candidate_basis: Named Pinus taeda canopy and Acer rubrum understory; plantation identity does not justify 100% pine ground area.
uncertainties: The forcing window 2005–2025 spans substantial thinning/regrowth; chronology and crown/LAI fractions must be period-matched. Pure-pine statements from limited immediate vicinity or models do not characterize all canopy strata.
next_evidence: Full BADM species/cover census, pre/post-2009-thinning inventory and later rotation history; separate overstory basal area, understory LAI and ground fractions.

vegetation: Subalpine conifer forest of Abies lasiocarpa, Picea engelmannii and Pinus contorta, selectively logged in early 1900s.
observed_composition: Seyednasrollah et al. report Abies lasiocarpa 46%, Picea engelmannii 28%, Pinus contorta 26% by stem density. Named species sum to 100% of reported stem-density accounting.
observed_pft_summary: Reported tree stems all evergreen needleleaf. This establishes an ENF tree-stem composition, not 100% site-area, ground-cover, LAI or vegetation-carbon fraction.
denominator: Tree stem density in stand description, not basal area or ground area.
observation_period: Site composition reported in 2021 paper; underlying tree census date not explicit. Separate pigment samples June 2017–June 2018 are not the abundance census.
spatial_scope: US-NR1 tower subalpine forest, approximately 3050 m elevation near Nederland, Colorado. Exact census extent not specified in cited paragraph.
bare_ground: Not quantified. No conversion of 100% tree-stem PFT share into 0% bare ground.
source_title: AmeriFlux US-NR1 site overview; Seyednasrollah et al. (2021), Seasonal variation in the canopy color of temperate evergreen conifer forests, New Phytologist 229:2586–2600, doi:10.1111/nph.17046
source_locator: Official Overview Description; Seyednasrollah p. 2588 (PDF p. 3), Materials and Methods, Niwot Ridge paragraph explicitly states stem density for each percentage.
candidate_pft: Evergreen needleleaf tree pool; boreal/temperate FATES subtype must be checked against the actual parameter set and species trait choices. No ground-area vector proposed.
candidate_basis: Reported tree species and stem shares, all evergreen conifers; 46/28/26 can be retained as species-level observed stem proportions only.
uncertainties: Stem density differs from BA, canopy cover and carbon weighting. Site ecotone and footprint direction vary; date and exact spatial extent of abundance census are missing from paragraph.
next_evidence: Retrieve US-NR1 inventory census provenance, size distribution, basal-area/crown cover and understory/ground survey before parameterizing area fractions or comparing with FATES VEGC shares.

vegetation: Snow-scoured alpine tundra. Official site identifies dry meadow; T-Van papers describe a mosaic of wind-scoured fellfield and dry meadow with small wet-meadow patches in tower footprints.
observed_composition: No site-specific numeric PFT/species cover vector verified. Regional dry-meadow sedge dominance and historical Niwot growth-form tables are not substituted for the exact US-NR3 tower footprint.
observed_pft_summary: Alpine C3 herbaceous graminoids/forbs with possible dwarf shrubs and nonvascular vegetation; detailed footprint shares unresolved.
denominator: None: vegetation-community descriptions; no area fractions read for the exact tower footprint.
observation_period: Tower since 2007; official overview current at retrieval; cited T-Van synthesis published 2017.
spatial_scope: T-Van West tower at 40.0520 N, 105.5864 W, official elevation 3504 m; US-NR4 only 50 m east. Small-scale alpine heterogeneity makes US-NR3/NR4 or Saddle extrapolation unsafe.
bare_ground: Not quantified. Snow-scoured/fellfield landscape can have rock/bare surfaces, but neither GRA nor regional cover supports 0% bare ground or a fixed number.
